info.title: SMS Rates
info.description:
JSONAPI interface to the SMS prices of a DIDWW account, in four price domains: what an SMS
sent through the account's A2P, P2P or OTP plan costs per destination (`sms_out/a2p`,
`sms_out/p2p`, `sms_out/otp`), and what an SMS arriving on one of the account's numbers
costs (`sms_in`), as priced by the plan the account is assigned to in each domain. The
plan's whole price list is one gzipped CSV file per domain; one number or one country is
looked up directly. Prices are plan values in USD, VAT excluded.

Every request is authenticated with a bearer access token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).
Mint one with `POST /token` on the token service of the environment you call —
`https://auth.didww.com/token` for Production, `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` for
Sandbox — with an API key issued in the DIDWW user panel. The audience this service verifies
is `api-sms.didww.com` on the production and on the sandbox host alike, so the token's `aud`
must list that name. Every operation here reads: a token minted with the `read` scope is
enough.

An account that holds no price plan of this service in a domain -- no plan at all, or a plan
this service publishes no prices for -- is answered with 404 `price_plan_not_assigned` by
every operation of that domain, and every operation spends the account's rate-limit budget:
once it is spent, the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`.

tags.name: Prices
tags.description: Price files and price lookups, served by the platform service that prices the traffic: Voice IN, Voice OUT, SMS.

bearer_token.description: Short-lived access token minted by `POST /token` on the token service of the environment you call — `https://auth.didww.com/token` for the Production servers, `https://auth-sandbox.didww.com/token` for the Sandbox servers — with an API key of that environment; a token minted in one environment is refused by the other. It is minted for an explicit set of audiences (`aud`). The audience of an operation is the production hostname of the server in effect for it — the Production entry of the operation's own `servers`, else of its path item's `servers` with the `service` variable resolved, else of the document's root `servers` — and it is the same name whether you call the production or the sandbox host. A service accepts a token only when `aud` lists its name: mint one token per service, or one token listing every service you call.

code.description: JSONAPI error code: a numeric code for a request-shape error (`100` a validation error, `102` a disallowed filter, `106` a missing parameter, and so on), the HTTP status for a refused token or scope (`401`, `403` — the reason is in `title` and in the `WWW-Authenticate` header), or a named code for a domain refusal or a serving failure (`price_plan_not_assigned`, `price_not_found`, `too_many_requests`, `serving_failure`).

source.description: Points at the part of the request that caused the error. Present on validation errors.

meta.description: Error-specific details. Carried by a few errors (e.g. insufficient balance).

id.description: UUID derived from the content of the answering row: the same across requests and regenerations while the row is unchanged, and distinct for distinct rows. A change to the row, its price included, gives it a new id, so the id does not follow the price of a destination over time. A name, not an address: there is no member route to fetch it by.

source_prefix.description: Prefix of the sending number the row is priced for; null when the row prices an SMS from any number.

destination_prefix.description: Destination prefix the row is priced for; with `filter[dst_number]`, the longest one covering the number among the rows the filters admit. Null when the row prices any destination.

country.description: Destination country the row is priced for, by name; null when the row is not attributed to a country.

mcc.description: Mobile country code of the destination network the row is priced for; null when the row prices any network.

mcc_name.description: Name of the mobile country code; null when `mcc` is.

mnc.description: Mobile network code of the destination network the row is priced for; null when the row prices any network of the country.

mnc_name.description: Name of the mobile network; null when `mnc` is.

reject_sms.description: True when the plan rejects SMS to this destination instead of pricing them; `price` is then null. A rejection is an answer, not a missing price.

price.description: Price per SMS in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string with six decimals; null when `reject_sms` is set.

data.description: Every row of the plan the filters select -- the rows of the winning prefix when a number is given, every row of the country otherwise. Rows equal in every stored value are answered once; two rows can still print alike, since they can differ in plan settings this API does not print and prices are printed to six decimals, and their ids then differ. Never empty: no answer is the 404 `price_not_found`.

A change to the row, its price included, gives it a new id, so the id does not follow the price of a destination over time. A name, not an address: there is no member route to fetch it by.

source_prefix.description: Prefix of the sending number the row is priced for; null when the row prices an SMS from any number.

source_number_length_min.description: Shortest sending number, in digits, the row is priced for.

source_number_length_max.description: Longest sending number, in digits, the row is priced for.

destination_prefix.description: Prefix of the receiving number the row is priced for; with `filter[dst_number]`, the longest one covering the number among the rows the filters admit whose length range holds it. Null when the row prices any destination.

destination_number_length_min.description: Shortest receiving number, in digits, the row is priced for.

destination_number_length_max.description: Longest receiving number, in digits, the row is priced for.

country.description: Country of the receiving number the row is priced for, by name; null when the row is not attributed to a country.

price.description: Price per SMS in USD, VAT excluded, as a decimal string with six decimals.

data.description: Every row of the plan the filters select -- the rows of the winning prefix whose destination length range holds the number when a number is given, every row of the country otherwise. Rows equal in every stored value are answered once; prices are printed to six decimals, so two rows can still print alike. Never empty: no answer is the 404 `price_not_found`.

ContentDisposition.description: `attachment` with the canonical file name of the price domain.

ContentLength.description: Size of the gzipped file in bytes; a HEAD answers the size the download sends.

LastModified.description: HTTP date the file's content or the account's plan assignment last changed; the value to send back in `If-Modified-Since`.

CacheControl.description: Always `private`: the file is served per account.

AcceptRanges.description: Always `none`: the file is served whole.

Vary.description: Always `Authorization`: one URL answers every account with its own plan's file.

get.summary: Look up the SMS OUT A2P prices of a number or a country
get.description: Looks up the SMS OUT A2P prices of one number or one country in the plan assigned to the account in this domain. With `filter[dst_number]` the number is matched against the destination prefixes of the plan: the longest prefix covering it wins, and every row of the plan under that prefix answers. Rows under one prefix can differ by the sending number they price (`source_prefix`), by the destination network (`mcc` and `mnc`, which only the delivery decides) and by plan settings this API does not print, so the collection is the plan rows that apply, not the one price charged. A destination the plan rejects is still an answer: `reject_sms` is true and `price` is null. With `filter[dst_country_iso]` alone, every row of the plan priced for that country answers, under every prefix; with both, the country narrows the rows before the prefixes are ranked. At least one of the two filters is required, and the collection is never empty -- a number no row of the plan covers, or a country the plan does not price, is a 404 (`price_not_found`). The token must list `api-sms.didww.com` in its audience, on the sandbox host as well; the `read` scope suffices. `filter` is the only query parameter read: `sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` and anything unrecognised are refused with 400.

parameters.name: filter[dst_number]
parameters.description: The number to price: 8 to 15 digits with a non-zero first digit, in international format without a `+` or a dialling prefix. Required unless `filter[dst_country_iso]` is sent.

parameters.name: filter[dst_country_iso]
parameters.description: The destination country, as its upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Alone, every row of the plan priced for that country answers; beside a number, only the rows of that country take part in the match. Required unless `filter[dst_number]` is sent.

200.description: the prices covering the number, or the prices of the country: every row of the plan the filters select, as the collection schema describes

400.description: malformed request: neither `filter[dst_number]` nor `filter[dst_country_iso]` sent; `filter[dst_number]` not 8 to 15 digits with a non-zero first digit; `filter[dst_country_iso]` not the upper-case code of a known country; a filter other than these two, `filter[id]` included; or any other query parameter -- `sort`, `page`, `fields`, `include` and anything unrecognised

401.description: the bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of; the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`

403.description: the token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`); the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`

404.description: the account holds no price plan of this service in this domain -- no plan at all, or a plan this service publishes no prices for (`price_plan_not_assigned`) -- or no row of the plan matches the filters (`price_not_found`)

429.description: the request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

get.summary: Download the SMS OUT A2P price file
get.description: Downloads the SMS OUT A2P price file of the plan assigned to the account in this domain: the prices of the plan as a gzipped CSV (UTF-8, LF line endings, a header row), named `sms_out_a2p_prices.csv.gz`, one row per rate of the plan with the columns Source prefix, Destination prefix, Country, MCC, MCC name, MNC, MNC name, Reject SMS and Price (USD, excl. VAT); Reject SMS is `Yes` with an empty price for a destination the plan rejects, `No` otherwise. An empty prefix prices any number, an empty MCC any network and an empty MNC any network of the country, as the nulls of the lookup do; the file leaves out some settings of a row, so two rows can look alike or show one destination at different prices; prices carry six decimals. The file is served whole, with no byte ranges, and it is the account's own: `Cache-Control` is `private` and `Vary` is `Authorization`, so a cache keyed by the URL alone must not hand it to another account. The token must list `api-sms.didww.com` in its audience, on the sandbox host as well; the `read` scope suffices. Conditional requests use `Last-Modified` and `If-Modified-Since` only: no `ETag` is sent, and a request carrying `If-None-Match` is always answered in full, its `If-Modified-Since` ignored. `Last-Modified` is the later of the last change of the file's content and the last change of the account's plan assignment in this domain, so an account moved to another plan is never answered 304 with the prices it left; send it back in `If-Modified-Since` to be answered 304 while nothing has changed.

parameters.name: If-Modified-Since
parameters.description: The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The file is sent only if it changed after that date; otherwise the answer is 304. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`.

304.description: the file has not changed since the `If-Modified-Since` date: the headers of the 200 and no body

401.description: the bearer token was refused: absent, malformed, expired, signed by a key this service does not hold, minted for another audience or environment, presented from an address outside the IP allowlist of the API key it was minted with, or naming an account this service has no record of; the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`

403.description: the token does not carry the `read` scope (title `Insufficient scope`); the response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`

404.description: the account holds no price plan of this service in this domain (`price_plan_not_assigned`): no plan at all, or a plan this service publishes no prices for

429.description: the request budget of the account for the current window is spent (`too_many_requests`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

503.description: the file could not be served: the assigned plan has no generated file yet, or the store did not answer for it (`serving_failure`); `Retry-After` says how many seconds to wait

head.summary: Check the SMS OUT A2P price file
head.description: Answers the headers of the SMS OUT A2P price file without its body -- `Last-Modified`, `Content-Disposition` with `sms_out_a2p_prices.csv.gz`, `Content-Length` and the cache headers of the download -- so a client can tell whether its copy is current before downloading. `If-Modified-Since` works as on the download: a date at or after `Last-Modified` is answered 304, unless the request also carries `If-None-Match`. The audience (`api-sms.didww.com`, the same on the sandbox host), the scope (`read`) and the refusals are those of the download; no response carries a body.

parameters.description: The `Last-Modified` date of the copy you hold. The headers of the file are answered only if it changed after that date; otherwise the answer is 304. Ignored when the request also carries `If-None-Match`.

200.description: the headers of the price file
